onboarding.headline:
Your Ledger,
Your Freedom.
onboarding.subtitle: Privacy first. Gimbo transforms your financial management into a silent, secure editorial experience.
onboarding.introBody: Before you start, it's worth understanding what makes Gimbo different from the finance apps you've used before.
onboarding.introPoint1Body: Your transactions are saved locally, in a database inside your own browser — not on a cloud server.
onboarding.introPoint2Body: That data can be exported as a .db file, like a spreadsheet: you decide where to keep it and where to take it.
onboarding.introPoint3Body: We don't ask for a login or send anything off your device. If you clear your browser data without exporting first, it's gone — that's why backups matter.

welcome.title: Welcome to Gimbo
welcome.subtitle: Before you start, understand how your data is protected
welcome.privacyBody: Gimbo has no servers. Everything is stored on your device, in the browser's IndexedDB. No financial data travels over the internet.
welcome.riskTitle: Warning: browser storage can be erased
welcome.riskBody: Clearing history, switching browsers, or reinstalling your OS can silently erase your data. We recommend setting up a local folder backup for extra safety.

demo.banner: Demo mode — changes are not saved

whyBrowserStorage.title: Why is browser storage fragile?
whyBrowserStorage.subtitle: Understand the risks of IndexedDB and how to protect your data
whyBrowserStorage.section1Body: By default, Gimbo saves your data in the browser's IndexedDB — a local database built into Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge. This ensures speed and full privacy: no server has access to your finances.
whyBrowserStorage.section2Body: The browser can erase IndexedDB data in several situations: when clearing browsing history and data, when using private/incognito mode, when uninstalling or reinstalling the browser, when switching browsers, or when the operating system reclaims disk space.
whyBrowserStorage.section3Body: By setting up a backup folder, Gimbo saves a copy of your vault on every auto-save. If you choose a folder inside Google Drive, Dropbox, or OneDrive, your data is automatically protected in the cloud — with no extra configuration.

backupLocal.title: Local folder backup
backupLocal.subtitle: How it works, permissions, and tips for using with Google Drive or Dropbox
backupLocal.section1Body: When you set up a backup folder, Gimbo uses the browser's File System Access API to write a copy of your database (gimbo-backup.db) to that folder on every auto-save. The file is identical to a manual export.
backupLocal.section2Body: For security reasons, the browser requires you to authorize folder access once per session. When you open Gimbo, if the authorization has expired, a notice will appear asking you to reconnect the folder. This is normal and takes just one click.
backupLocal.section3Title: Using with Google Drive, Dropbox, or OneDrive
backupLocal.section3Body: If you choose a folder synced by Google Drive, Dropbox, or OneDrive, the service's desktop app detects the new file and uploads it to the cloud automatically. This keeps your data protected with no API configuration or additional account in Gimbo.
backupLocal.section4Body: Local folder backup (without multi-device mode) always writes the same file, gimbo-backup.db. If you use that same synced folder on two computers with Gimbo open at the same time, the cloud client doesn't know how to merge the changes — it silently creates a duplicate conflict copy (e.g. gimbo-backup (1).db) without warning that the data diverged. On mobile devices, the browser also doesn't expose the file system the same way, so this backup only works on the computer where it was set up.
backupLocal.section5Body: Turn on "Sync between my computers" in Settings → Backup & Sync to use Gimbo on more than one computer with the same shared folder. Each computer then writes exclusively its own file (device-<id>.db) — never another device's file — which eliminates the conflict copy by construction: no file ever has two writers. On open, each computer reads the others' files and merges the changes automatically. Don't edit, move, or rename the device-*.db files by hand; use "Remove this device" in Settings to retire a computer you no longer use. This mode is desktop-only — mobile still depends on Cloud Sync (Fase 2, see the next page).

cloudSync.title: Cloud Sync
cloudSync.subtitle: Sync with Google Drive — Dropbox not available yet
cloudSync.section1Body: In Settings → Backup & Sync, connect your Google Drive account (two clicks, OAuth2 — Gimbo never sees your password, and only ever touches a file it creates itself). The app keeps a "Gimbo" folder in your Drive with a single gimbo.db file synced against your local vault. This is what finally unlocks mobile use: the mobile browser has no access to the local file system the way Fase 1's multi-device mode requires.
cloudSync.section2Body: If you only sync between computers (not mobile), multi-device mode (Backup & Sync → "Sync between my computers") covers that without OAuth — see the Local Folder Backup page. Cloud Sync talks directly to Google's API, so it works even without the Google Drive desktop client installed, and it's the only option that also covers mobile.
cloudSync.section3Body: Cloud Sync via Google Drive is already implemented, but it only shows up in Settings if this Gimbo installation has the Google connection configured (a one-time setup done by the project maintainer, not by you). If the "Connect Google Drive" button isn't there, use multi-device mode (Fase 1) or manual backup in the meantime. Dropbox (Fase 3) hasn't been implemented yet.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Gimbo is a local-first personal finance app. All your financial data is stored exclusively on your device. We do not operate our own servers and do not collect any personal data.
privacy.s1Body: No data is transmitted to Gimbo servers. The information you enter — name, email, and financial transactions — is saved locally in your browser's IndexedDB and never leaves your device without your explicit action.
privacy.s2Body: Gimbo uses IndexedDB to persist your financial data and the Service Worker cache to store app files. This data resides entirely on your device and is subject to your browser's privacy policies.
privacy.s3Body: Gimbo does not integrate ad networks, behavioral analytics, or tracking services. The published version is hosted on Vercel, which may log access metadata (IP address, timestamp) per its own privacy policy.
privacy.s4Body: You have full control over your data. You can export it at any time from the Settings screen and delete it permanently through your browser. Gimbo has no remote access to your data.
privacy.s5Body: Questions about this policy can be sent to fabiodassan@gmail.com.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.intro: By using Gimbo, you agree to the following terms. Please read them carefully.
terms.s1Body: Gimbo is a free personal finance web app available as a PWA. It requires no account creation and does not depend on proprietary servers to function.
terms.s2Body: You are solely responsible for the custody and backup of your financial data. Gimbo provides export tools but does not perform automatic cloud backups. Data lost due to browser cache clearing cannot be recovered by Gimbo.
terms.s3Body: All data you enter in Gimbo belongs to you. Gimbo claims no rights over your data and cannot access it remotely.
terms.s4Body: Gimbo is provided "as is," without express or implied warranties of fitness for any purpose, continuous availability, or freedom from errors.

origin.title: What is Gimbo?
origin.intro: "Gimbo" is a word from Brazilian Portuguese, with roots in Bantu languages, historically used as a synonym for money. The app's name is a nod to that linguistic heritage — and to a classic Brazilian song.
origin.s1Body: According to Dicio (Dicionário Online de Português), "gimbo" is a masculine noun, used informally and regionally in Brazil, meaning money. The word entered Brazilian Portuguese through the Bantu languages brought by enslaved African peoples during the colonial period.
origin.s2Title: Jimbo, zimbo, and currency in colonial Brazil
origin.s2Body: The "zimbo" (also spelled "jimbo") was a shell currency used in trade along the African coast, and it was also adopted as a unit of value in colonial Brazil alongside metal coins such as the florin. "Gimbo" is a variant of that same root, and over time it came to broadly mean money in popular Brazilian vocabulary.
